results.title: LIVE from Ireland: Hugh Fagan on trial for sitting on a bench with signs
results.description: Subhead:He doesn't shout, block anyone or ask for anything. He sits in Wexford's town square with seven homemade signs, and the Irish state has charged him with a public order offence. Rebel News is inside Wexford District Court for the trial.# Hugh Fagan is in Wexford District Court, in the south-east of Ireland, charged with a public order offence over his homemade signs. Rebel News is covering it as it happens - live-tweeting from inside and filming outside. Follow along for updates below or directly on X. X-embed:https://x.com/ezralevant/status/2115045105338040594 X-embed:32 Hugh has refused to plead guilty. His barrister, Laoise de Brún, and solicitor, Padraig Langsch - the same legal team defending Kirk Loco in Bray - will fight the charge in open court. Hugh still may not know exactly what he's accused of: when asked which of his seven signs he was charged over, Hugh said police hadn't told him, and that he'd find out in court. Hugh lives in Wexford, a tourist town of cobbled streets, coffee shops and a medieval abbey. Most days he walks four blocks from his house to the town square and sits on a bench with seven handmade signs propped up around him. He wears headphones. He doesn't shout. He doesn't hand out leaflets or ask anyone for anything. He isn't a member of any party. If you want to talk, he takes the headphones off and talks to you. If you don't, he just sits there. It started in May of last year. Hugh was walking past a church near the Tesco on a Sunday as a funeral was coming out, the casket being put into the hearse, and a beggar was lying across the entrance. He said to himself, enough is enough. The next week he was in the square with two signs. Now there are seven - about mass immigration, churches being burned across Europe, the safety of women and children, and the European Union.
